title: How does limestone become marble? Quiz
description: After watching the episode on how Ipoh's rough grey limestone became smooth, shiny marble, do you know what baked it?

questions.question: How did Ipoh's limestone hills form in the first place?
options: From lava that erupted and cooled
Shells of tiny sea creatures and very fine mud piled up layer by layer on the seabed, then were pressed together
River sand stuck together by a natural glue
questions.explanation: Hundreds of millions of years ago the Ipoh area was a sea. Shells and fine mud, mostly made of calcite, settled on the seabed, piled up layer by layer and were pressed together into limestone.

questions.question: Does limestone have to melt and cool again to become marble?
options: Yes, it has to melt into magma first
No. Buried deep underground and heated and squeezed, its calcite grains slowly grow again and lock together
No, it just has to sit in water for a long time
questions.explanation: It never gets hot enough to melt, but with heat and pressure the calcite grains slowly regrow and lock together like a jigsaw. The gaps disappear and the rock turns dense and shiny, just as ice cubes in the freezer stick into one block without melting.

questions.question: What happens if you put a drop of vinegar on limestone and on marble?
questions.explanation: Both are made of calcite, so both fizz with an acid like vinegar. That's how you can tell they are really the same stuff.

questions.question: What heated Ipoh's limestone into marble?
options: Magma rising from deep underground that slowly cooled into granite right next to it
Hundreds of millions of years of hot Ipoh sun
The machines used in the old tin mines
questions.explanation: More than 200 million years ago, huge masses of hot magma cooled slowly into granite beneath and beside the limestone. Over that long time the limestone was like something left next to a big oven, and it slowly turned into marble.

questions.question: Why are shell fossils so hard to find in the hills around Ipoh?
options: The area was never under the sea
People have dug them all out
When the rock was heated, the fossils grew into crystals too
questions.explanation: Ordinary limestone often shows bits of shell, but Ipoh's hills were heated, and the fossils grew into the crystals along with everything else, so they can hardly be recognised now.
